answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks through Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent must generate a unique cryptographic proof from their hardware enclave. Second, they must deposit a $10,000 bond into a smart contract. Third, the protocol verifies the hardware identity against a global registry. Fourth, the node is whitelisted for tasks. An attacker would need $100,000 in bonds and 15 days of provisioning to spoof ten nodes. This prevents a parasitic vine from strangling the system. Every verified node is a relic of integrity, protecting the ember of consensus.
